concepts.title: Rutherford Scattering and the Nuclear Atom
concepts.definition: Firing alpha particles at a thin gold foil showed most sailing straight through while roughly one in eight thousand bounced back past 90 degrees, which only makes sense if the positive charge and nearly all the mass sit in a minute central nucleus.
concepts.formula: impact parameter b sets the scattering angle
concepts.key_idea: Atoms are mostly empty space; head-on approaches to the nucleus produce the rare large deflections.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph204.txt section 12.2 (Geiger-Marsden experiment, 0.14 percent beyond 1 degree, impact parameter)

solution_steps.explain: most alpha particles meet nothing solid, so they sail through the foil

concepts.title: Distance of Closest Approach
concepts.definition: A head-on alpha particle halts for an instant when all its kinetic energy sits as electrostatic potential energy, and that turning point fixes the closest distance it ever gets to the nucleus.
concepts.key_idea: The closest approach caps the nucleus radius from above, since the particle turns back before touching it.

concepts.title: Total Energy of the Orbiting Electron
concepts.definition: A Rutherford electron in a stable circle carries negative total energy: the potential part is exactly twice the kinetic part but opposite in sign, leaving E equal to minus the Coulomb term over twice the orbit radius.
concepts.key_idea: The negative sign is the binding: positive energy would let the electron escape instead of circling.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph204.txt section 12.2.2 (K, U and Eq. 12.4, Example 12.3)

solution_steps.action: form the Coulomb constant times e squared

concepts.title: Line Spectra as Atomic Fingerprints
concepts.definition: Excited thin gases radiate only at certain discrete wavelengths, printing bright emission lines, while a cool gas crossing white light deletes exactly those same wavelengths as dark absorption lines.
concepts.formula: emission lines = absorption lines of the same gas
concepts.key_idea: Each element's line pattern is unique, so spectra identify gases like fingerprints identify people.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph204.txt section 12.3 (emission and absorption line spectra)

concepts.title: Bohr Postulates of the Hydrogen Atom
concepts.definition: Bohr rescued the nuclear atom with three rules: electrons hold certain non-radiating stationary orbits, only orbits with angular momentum an integer times h over two pi are allowed, and jumps between orbits emit or absorb a photon carrying the energy gap.
concepts.key_idea: Quantised angular momentum plus the photon energy rule turn the runaway classical atom into a stable one with sharp spectral lines.

solution_steps.explain: in stationary states the electron circulates without emitting radiant energy
only orbits with L equal to n h over two pi survive
a drop between levels emits a photon with h nu equal to the energy difference

concepts.title: Energy of the nth Bohr Level
concepts.definition: The allowed energies of hydrogen collapse to one compact formula: the nth level carries minus 13.6 electron volts divided by n squared.
concepts.key_idea: Levels crowd toward zero as n grows, with n equals 1 the deepest state at -13.6 eV.

solution_steps.explain: the level energy falls off as one over n squared

concepts.title: Excitation Energy From the Ground State
concepts.definition: Raising hydrogen's electron from the ground state to level n costs the difference between the two level energies, and that cost shrinks as the target level climbs.
concepts.key_idea: First excitation takes 10.2 eV, second 12.09 eV, while ionisation needs the full 13.6 eV.

concepts.title: Bohr Orbit Radii
concepts.definition: Quantised angular momentum lets the electron occupy only certain circles, and each radius grows with the square of the quantum number starting from the Bohr radius near 5.3e-11 m.
concepts.key_idea: Doubling the level quadruples the orbit: radii run a0, 4 a0, 9 a0 and onward.

concepts.title: Electron Speed in a Bohr Orbit
concepts.definition: The orbital speed of hydrogen's electron falls off as one over the quantum number, topping out near 2.2 million metres per second in the ground orbit.
concepts.key_idea: Outer electrons travel slower, so higher levels mean longer, lazier circuits.

concepts.title: Photon Energy of a Level Transition
concepts.definition: When an electron drops from a higher level to a lower one, the freed energy difference leaves as a single photon, and in hydrogen that gap comes straight from the level formula.
concepts.key_idea: Only jumps, not spirals, produce light, and each jump owns one exact energy.

solution_steps.explain: the starting level carries -13.6 over n i squared

concepts.title: Photon Frequency From the Energy Gap
concepts.definition: Dividing a transition's energy gap by Planck's constant turns it into the frequency of the light the atom emits or absorbs, which is why spectra show sharp lines.
concepts.key_idea: Each level pair maps to exactly one frequency, filling the spectrum with discrete lines.

concepts.title: de Broglie Standing Waves on Bohr Orbits
concepts.definition: Bohr's quantisation stops looking arbitrary once the electron is a wave: a stable orbit is one whose circumference fits a whole number of de Broglie wavelengths, which recreates the n h over two pi rule.
concepts.key_idea: Only resonant standing particle waves persist on the orbit, so the allowed orbits are the constructive ones.
concepts.textbook_ref: leph204.txt section 12.6 (Eq. 12.12 and the standing wave picture)

solution_steps.action: wrap the wave on the circle
solution_steps.explain: a persistent orbit needs the wave to meet itself in phase after one lap

concepts.title: Quantum Numbers of Everyday Orbits
concepts.definition: Bohr's quantisation applied to a planet-scale orbit yields a quantum number in the ten-to-the-seventies, which is exactly why the graininess of angular momentum is never seen in daily life.
concepts.key_idea: Angular momentum steps of h over two pi are so minute that ordinary orbits sit unimaginably far up the ladder.

solution_steps.explain: for a circular orbit the angular momentum is m v r

for planetary data n lands near ten to the seventy-fourth, so adjacent levels are indistinguishable

solution_template.explain: for a circle the angular momentum is mass times speed times radius: 6e24 * 3e4 * 1.5e11 = 2.7e40 J s
